react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolome is dominated by arachidonic acid cascade lipids and sulfur amino-acid metabolites, yielding a clear cross-paradigm consensus on two interconnected pathways. Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) is the top-ranked hit in the RaMP multi-DB ORA (FDR = 6.18 × 10⁻¹⁴; fold enrichment 1 429; 5 of 5 input lipids detected across 27 pathway members). The same lipid set — arachidonic acid (C00219), leukotriene A4 (C00909), 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-prostaglandin J2 (C14717), 5(S)-HETE (C04805) and 15(S)-HETE (C04742) — defines the m/z-directed Arachidonic acid metabolism pathway in mummichog (p = 0.0015, rank 1, 11 of 11 pathway compounds matched) and appears as KEGG:hsa00590 in MetaboAnalystR (rank 1, raw p = 1.0 but full overlap on the four core eicosanoids). The second biological theme is sulfur amino-acid metabolism: L-cysteine (C00097) and L-cystathionine (C02291) drive significant enrichment in the methionine/cysteine KEGG pathways (hsa00670, hsa00260, hsa00270; raw p ≤ 0.0082) and map to the MUMM methionine-and-cysteine-metabolism module (rank 8, p = 0.0487). Mercaptopurine (C02380), the purine thiol drug, did not contribute to either pathway cluster, indicating it may reflect direct drug metabolism or an independent nucleotide perturbation. The convergent evidence across ORA (RaMP), m/z-network (mummichog) and KEGG-specific PSEA (MetaboAnalystR) establishes that the treatment strongly dysregulates the arachidonic acid → eicosanoid axis and the transsulfuration pathway, with arachidonic acid and its 5- and 15-lipoxygenase products serving as the primary driver metabolites.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) is the top-ranked hit in the RaMP multi-DB ORA with an FDR of 6.18 × 10⁻¹⁴ and a fold enrichment of 1429.66, with 5 of 5 eicosanoid input lipids matching 27 pathway members. Selenium micronutrient network (WP:WP15) is rank 2 in the same analysis (FDR = 6.18 × 10⁻¹⁴, fold enrichment = 417.31, 6 metabolites hit). Mummichog's m/z-network analysis returned Arachidonic acid metabolism (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism) as its top hit with p = 0.0013 and a perfect 11-of-11 overlap. The two biological themes are eicosanoid synthesis (dominated by arachidonic acid cascade lipids) and the selenium micronutrient network (which additionally captures L-cysteine and L-cystathionine). The MUMM Methionine and cysteine metabolism pathway (MUMM:methionine_and_cysteine_metabolism) has rank 8 with p = 0.052, containing L-cystathionine as a confirmed member. Mercaptopurine did not contribute to either the eicosanoid cluster or the selenium network. Arachidonic acid (KEGG:C00219) and leukotriene A4 (KEGG:C00909) are primary driver metabolites of the eicosanoid synthesis pathway; 5-HETE (KEGG:C04805) and 15-HETE (KEGG:C04742) provide additional support for the lipid cluster.
